title: Dominant characters occur on Borel-stable highest-weight lines
statement: Let $F$ be an algebraically closed field [def-weil-field, def-weil-algebraic-closure]. Let $G$ be a reductive $F$-group scheme [def-sc-group-scheme], meaning a smooth connected affine group scheme of finite type with no nontrivial smooth connected normal unipotent subgroup. Unipotent means that all geometric points are unipotent matrices in a faithful linear representation. Fix a split maximal torus $T$ and a Borel subgroup $B\supseteq T$ with unipotent radical $U$, projection $p:B\to T$, simple roots $\Delta$ and coroots as in [lem-sfb-reductive-borel-pair-structure]. Let $\lambda:T\to\mathbf G_m$ be a character with $\langle\lambda,\alpha^\vee\rangle\ge0$ for every $\alpha\in\Delta$, and put $\widetilde\lambda=\lambda\circ p$. There exist a nonzero finite-dimensional rational $G$-module $V$ and $0\ne v\in V$ such that $$b\cdot(v\otimes1)=\widetilde\lambda(b)(v\otimes1)\quad\text{for every commutative }F\text{-algebra }A\text{ and }b\in B(A).$$ Rational means that $V$ has an $F$-linear coaction $V\to V\otimes_F F[G]$ satisfying coassociativity and the counit identity, equivalently a group-scheme representation on $V$. The line $Fv$ is thus $B$-stable with character $\widetilde\lambda$ and $U$ acts trivially on it. This holds in every characteristic and for the trivial group.

source.place: Theorem 22.2 and 22.3 (pp.463--464), Proposition 22.17 and Theorem 22.20 (pp.467--468); positive system attached to B as in 21.35.

proof.text: First treat a semisimple simply connected group $S$ with the given Borel pair. For each fundamental character $\omega_i$, take the rational big-cell function $f_i=f_{\omega_i}$ and the integer $d_i>0$ and regular function $h_i$ supplied by the two cited inputs. Their restrictions satisfy $f_i^{d_i}=h_i$. Since both lie in $F(S)$ and restriction is injective, this equality holds in $F(S)$. Hence $f_i$ is integral over $F[S]$: it is a root of the monic polynomial $X^{d_i}-h_i$. Integral closedness gives $f_i\in F[S]$. It is nonzero, lies in $E_{B_S}(w_0\omega_i)$, and is fixed by $U_S$ with $T_S$-weight $\omega_i$, by the character-function input. Hence $bf_i=\widetilde\omega_i(b)f_i$ for $b\in B_S(A)$: write $b=ut$ with $u\in U_S(A)$ and $t=p_S(b)$, using $B_S=U_S\rtimes T_S$, so $bf_i=u(tf_i)=\omega_i(t)f_i$. No extraction of a field-theoretic root or division by $d_i$ is involved.

The space $E_{B_S}(w_0\omega_i)$ is the section space of the homogeneous invertible coherent sheaf $\mathcal L_{w_0\omega_i}$ on $S/B_S$. The quotient is proper and finite type over $F$. Apply proper coherent cohomology finiteness to $S/B_S\to\operatorname{Spec}F$ in degree zero; its Noetherian base is the spectrum of a field. Thus this is a finite-dimensional rational $S$-module $V_i$. It contains the nonzero $f_i$ from step 1. The character-function input gives the rational action, so finite dimensionality here does not assert semisimplicity in positive characteristic.

source.place: Lemma 22.25; Section 18c and Definition 22.21; proper coherent finiteness Stacks Tags 02O5, 02O6.

proof.text: For any dominant character $\mu$ of $T_S$, write $\mu=\sum_i m_i\omega_i$ using the weight-lattice basis; $m_i=\langle\mu,\alpha_i^\vee\rangle\ge0$. Set $V_S=\bigotimes_i V_i^{\otimes m_i}$ and $v_S=\bigotimes_i f_i^{\otimes m_i}$. Tensor the coactions; the Hopf multiplication gives the diagonal action and coassociativity follows from its multiplicativity. The module is finite-dimensional. Choose linear forms taking each $f_i$ to $1$; their tensor product takes $v_S$ to $1$, so $v_S\ne0$. For every $F$-algebra $A$, the diagonal action gives $b v_S=\prod_i\widetilde\omega_i(b)^{m_i}v_S=\widetilde\mu(b)v_S$. Empty tensor products are $F$ and $1$; thus this also handles $S=1$ and $\mu=0$.

source.place: Lemma 22.26 and final proof of Theorem 22.20, printed p.470.

proof.text: For general $G$, take the faithfully flat cover $q:H=Z\times_F S\to G$ with finite central kernel, $Z=\mathbf G_m^r$ a split torus and $S$ semisimple simply connected. The group $H$ is smooth, connected, affine and of finite type: $H\to S$ is smooth by the torus-projection node, hence $H\to\operatorname{Spec}F$ is smooth by composition with the smooth $S$; the same node makes $L[\mathbf Z^r]$ a domain for every field $L\supseteq F$, so $Z$ is geometrically connected and the product-components node makes $H$ connected; $F[H]=F[Z]\otimes_FF[S]$ is finitely generated. So the compatibility node applies; it makes $H$ reductive. Lift the specified Borel pair using it, obtaining $B_H=Z\times B_S$, $T_H=Z\times T_S$ and $K=\ker(q)\subseteq T_H$. Write $q_T^*\lambda=(\eta,\mu)$, where $\eta$ and $\mu$ are its restrictions to the two factors: a character on a product is their product because $(z,t)=(z,1)(1,t)$. Pairing compatibility makes $\mu$ dominant. Apply step 3 to $S$ and $\mu$ and let $Z$ act by the one-dimensional character $\eta$. The resulting finite-dimensional rational $H$-module $V$ contains $v=1\otimes v_S\ne0$ with $B_H$-character $q^*\widetilde\lambda$; this follows from compatibility of the Borel projections and the diagonal action. Since $K\subseteq B_H$ and $q|_K=1$, its full scheme-theoretic action fixes $v$.

source.place: Final proof of Theorem 22.20; Proposition 21.60 and 22.12, pp.442,465,470.

proof.text: Take the rational $H$-submodule $W$ generated by $v$. The descent node makes it a finite-dimensional rational $G$-module on the same vector space, with $v\ne0$. The $B$-eigenvector identity can be tested after the faithfully flat cover $B_H\to B$. Concretely, for $b\in B(A)$ form the nonzero faithfully flat $A$-algebra $A'$ of its pullback torsor, over which $b$ has a lift $b_H$. Step 4 gives $b v=\widetilde\lambda(b)v$ in $W\otimes_F A'$. Faithful flatness detects equality, so the identity holds in $W\otimes_F A$. (For $A=0$ it is immediate.) This proves the required identity for every $A$. As $\widetilde\lambda|_U=1$, $U$ acts trivially on $Fv$; and the scalar identity proves that this line is $B$-stable. For $G=1$ all constructions reduce to $W=F$, $v=1$.
